info.title: Toolpath Engine API
info.description:
Public REST API for Toolpath engine operations.

**Units.** All dimensional values — in parts and in feature details — are in
millimetres; all angles are in degrees. Each part response also states this in its `units` field.

**Browser use.** CORS is per API key: a request only receives an
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header when its `Origin` is in the allowlist configured on the
key used (set when creating or editing the key in the portal). A key with no allowed origins
is server-to-server only. A Bearer API key placed in client-side JavaScript is readable by
anyone — restrict its origins, prefer a `read_only` key (read_only keys may call GET
operations only; writes are rejected with 403), or proxy requests through your own server.

tags.name: Holders
tags.description: Tool holder upload, import, and collision-envelope operations.

ApiKeyAuth.description: A Toolpath API key supplied as a Bearer credential.

Turnability.description: Whether the part belongs on a lathe; narrow on `kind`.

kind.description: Discriminator identifying a part with no turning axis.
Discriminator identifying a part with a turning axis.

direction.description: Direction of the turning axis, as a unit vector.

location.description: Point on the turning axis, in mm. Purely radial: its projection onto the axis is zero.

areaFraction.description: Fraction of the part’s surface area a turning setup about this axis could finish, from 0 to 1 — the area lying on the part’s envelope of revolution within tolerance.

volumeFraction.description: Fraction of the part’s envelope of revolution — what comes off the lathe — that the part keeps, from 0 to 1. The rest is what a turning setup leaves to be cut away some other way, so a radially unbalanced part scores low here however much of its surface lies on the envelope.

areas.description: What the surface is made of, as a partition that sums to the feature's area.

pinchPoints.description:
The places the feature is at its tightest: where the clearance reaches the minimum
`cd` reports, one disc per stretch of the feature that reaches it, tightest first
and never more than ten.

The counterpart of a bound rather than another bound: what these answer is *where*
the clearance minimum was decided, which the number itself cannot. A drawing is the
audience, which is why the list is capped — a feature can tie in dozens of places,
and the eleventh disc tells a reader nothing the first ten did not.

Empty for the kinds whose clearance is not measured off a single medial axis — a
hole, a facing pass, the undercut and layered kinds — so empty is "nowhere to point
at", never "nowhere is tight".

holderId.description: Identifier of the newly created holder.

status.description: Initial state of the accepted import job.

importId.description: Identifier of this immutable holder result.

jobId.description: Identifier of the import job that produced this holder result.

kernelVersion.description: Version of the Toolpath kernel that produced this holder result.

units.description: Units used by all dimensional values in this holder response.

options.description: The import options this result was produced with.

layers.description: The collision envelope as a stack of cones, nose first — the solid the holder sweeps as the spindle turns it, not the modeled solid. Wrench flats, coolant bores and nut slots are inside it by construction. Always the complete envelope, taper included; a gauge-plane cut is an export option on `GET /v1/holders/{id}/fusion`.

gaugeLength.description: Distance from the bottom of the stack to the gauge plane, in mm, or null when it was not measured. Null is not zero: a straight shank or a Capto carries no cone to place a gauge plane on.

sizeClass.description: The spindle taper’s nominal size — 30, 40 or 50 for a 7:24, one of 25 through 160 for an HSK — or null when no taper was found. A size, not a holder: geometry cannot tell BT40 from CAT40 from ISO40.

taperFamily.description: Which interface `sizeClass` belongs to, or null when no taper was found. Read the two together: an HSK40 and an ISO40 are both 40 and are otherwise nothing alike.

axisDirection.description: The axis the holder turns about, as a unit vector in the file’s coordinates. Its sign is arbitrary — it says nothing about which end goes in the spindle. The holder runs nose to spindle along it unless `flipped`.

axisLocation.description: A point on that axis, purely radial. With `nose` it is what puts the layer stack back on the geometry it was measured from.

nose.description: Where the holder’s nose sits, in the file’s coordinates. The layer stack starts here.

axisAreaFraction.description: Share of the file’s surface area carried by faces agreeing on the axis, or null when not measured. Low is a warning: a holder something is wrong with, not a holder measured badly.

faceCount.description: Faces across every body in the file — evidence the holder arrived intact rather than as the three faces of a failed translation.

sampleCount.description: Envelope bins before simplification. Against the length of `layers` it says how much of the holder was groove detail.

flipped.description: Whether the file models the holder spindle-end first.

taperAtNose.description: Whether the taper sits at the nose end of the stack instead of the spindle end, which happens only when the `flipped` option turned the holder away from the detected cone.

meshPointCount.description: Number of points in the generated envelope mesh.

meshTriangleCount.description: Number of triangles in the generated envelope mesh.

thumbnailUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the rendered PNG thumbnail, or null when absent.

meshStlUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the generated STL envelope mesh, or null when absent.

meshGlbUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the generated GLB envelope mesh, or null when absent.

fusionAvailable.description: Whether an Autodesk Fusion holder definition is available for download at `GET /v1/holders/{id}/fusion`.

fusionTrimmedAvailable.description: Whether that download can serve an envelope cut at the gauge plane. False when there was nothing to cut at — no gauge plane was measured, or a flip put the taper at the nose — in which case `trim=true` serves the complete envelope.

angleDeg.description:
Between the bevel's surface and the tool axis, degrees: zero for a wall, a right
angle for a floor. A matching tool's cone half angle is this.

slant.description:
How far the bevel runs along its own slope — the length of cutting edge a tool
needs to span it in one pass.

lowerAdjacentZMin.description:
The highest bottom among the features the bevel stands on — how far down there
is room under it before a tool would meet something. z grows up the tool axis,
so this is *below* the bevel's own `zMin` by the room there is.

isOpenPocketBottom.description: The bevel breaks the edge along an open pocket's floor.

countersink.description: Present only when the bevel is a countersink of revolution.

BevelFacts.description:
The bevel itself: how it leans, how far it runs, and what its surroundings allow a
cone to overshoot.

cd.description: Clearance-diameter limits for tools sweeping around the boss.

maxBottomDiameter.description: Largest bottom diameter a terminal tool may have, in mm.

wallLength.description:
The outline a pass around the wall follows, sized for any tool. Absent where the
projection left no outline — a wall nothing can price, not one that is free.

filletRadius.description: Radius of the floor blend, in mm; zero when sharp.

filletHeight.description: Height of the floor blend, in mm; zero when sharp.

BossFacts.description: A boss: a pocket turned inside out — material with void around it.

min.description: Largest tool diameter that reaches every point of the feature, in mm.

max.description: Largest tool diameter that fits somewhere in the feature, in mm.

CdBounds.description:
How wide a tool a feature admits — two upper bounds, differing in how much of the
feature the tool has to reach. `min` is the largest tool that reaches every part of
the feature, `max` the largest that fits somewhere; `min <= max`. Infinities are
meaningful — see `CdBounds` in the `api` crate for the three sentinel states.

ignore.description: Clearance-diameter bounds while deviations in the ignored tolerance band are allowed.

deviate.description: Clearance-diameter bounds while deviations in the reported tolerance band are allowed.

effectiveAdaptive.description: Clearance-diameter bounds after adaptive-cutting allowances are applied.

terminalCornerRadius.description:
The corner radius a terminal tool must not exceed; negative infinity when
unconstrained.

CdData.description: Clearance-diameter bounds per tolerance regime, plus the flags derived with them.

bevel.description: Measurements for machining the chamfer with a conical tool flank.

three.description: Measurements for machining the chamfer as a followable surface.

ChamferFacts.description:
A chamfer, which is two things at once and carries a measurement of each: a bevel
cut by a cone's flank, and a surface a ball can follow. Which one a given tool
answers to is settled by the tool's own shape.

taperDeg.description:
Between the overhanging wall and the tool axis, degrees, positive however the
wall leans.

filletRadius.description: Radius of the blend between wall and floor; 0.0 for the sharp kind.

floorWidth.description: The widest clearance over the floor — the width the groove cuts at.

topOpeningWidth.description: The clearance through the opening at the top of the groove.

bottomOpeningWidth.description: The clearance just above the floor, under the overhangs.

isExternal.description:
The groove's inner clearances vary from place to place — it runs out somewhere —
rather than being the one constant width a closed internal dovetail has.

cd.description:
Derived from the widths and the taper, not measured off an axis, so the three
regimes hold one answer.

isInvalidGeometry.description:
A width could not be measured at all, so `cd` is arithmetic over a zero and no
tool should be offered on its strength.

DovetailFacts.description:
A dovetail groove: overhanging walls leaning back at one angle over a floor, so the
space widens with depth and a tool has to enter through an opening narrower than where
it cuts.

That inversion is why this carries widths rather than a medial-axis measurement. All
three are clearance diameters read at their own heights, with `0.0` standing for a
measurement that failed — which is what `isInvalidGeometry` reports.

isTopFace.description: The face is the highest surface of the part along the tool axis.

isFacing.description: The face is to be faced off: a top face the fixture does not rule out.

needsSidemill.description: Sweeping the floor does not clear the face on its own — a wall pass must follow.

cd.description: Clearance-diameter limits for tools sweeping the face.

maxBottomDiameter.description: Largest bottom diameter a terminal tool may have, in mm.

FaceFacts.description: A face: a plane square to the tool axis, cleared by sweeping across it.

FeatureType.description:
What kind of thing a feature is, and so how it gets machined. The names are the
contract at this boundary (the shared numeric wire format stays inside the binary
API).

diameter.description:
What the hole is actually drilled to — narrower than modelled for a threaded
hole.

fullConeDeg.description: Full apex angle of the cone at the hole bottom, degrees; 180 for a flat bottom.

isCounterbore.description: Whether the hole includes a larger counterbore at its mouth.

holeProcess.description: The requested machining process for this hole.

threading.description: The thread this hole is to receive and how it is cut; absent for a plain hole.

cd.description: Clearance-diameter limits for tools entering the hole.

maxSpotDiameter.description: Largest spot-drill diameter that reaches the hole without collision, in mm.

maxDrillDiameter.description: Largest drill diameter that leaves the hole within its permitted oversize, in mm.

maxEndmillDiameter.description: Largest end-mill diameter that can machine the hole, in mm.

filletRadius.description: Radius of the blend at the hole bottom, in mm; zero when sharp.

filletHeight.description: Height of the bottom blend, in mm; zero when sharp.

HoleFacts.description: A hole's facts. See `HoleFacts` in the `api` crate for what each figure means.

HoleProcess.description: How the user wants a hole machined.

length.description: The outline's own length, in mm — what a pass would travel with a tool of no width.

dlDr.description:
How the travelled length changes per mm of tool radius: the outline's total signed
turning, in radians and so dimensionless. Negative around an outline a tool runs
inside of, positive around one it runs outside of, and `±2π` where the outline closes.

OffsetLength.description:
An outline a pass follows, measured so that any tool's path length can be read off it.

A pass does not walk the outline: it walks the tool *center*, offset by the tool radius to
the free side, which is shorter than the outline inside a pocket and longer around a boss.
So the length a tool of `radius` travels is `Math.max(0, length + radius * dlDr)`, and zero
means the tool does not fit — the outline is shorter than the tool's own orbit, which a
caller pricing a pass must refuse rather than bill as free.

Exact for every tool the outline has room for, except at a corner sharper than the tool,
where it reads long by that corner's miter — zero for the filleted corners a pocket that
admits the tool is made of.

center.description: The disc's center, across the part rather than along the tool.

diameter.description:
The disc's diameter, which is the clearance there — the datasheet's minimum
clearance diameter, up to the tolerance it was measured at.

PinchPoint.description:
Where a feature is at its tightest: one place its clearance reaches the minimum, as the
disc that measures it.

The disc fits in the space the clearance was measured in and touches the feature
boundary, so a cylinder of `diameter` standing at `center` and spanning the datasheet's
`zMin`..`zMax` is exactly the widest tool that reaches the boundary there — which is what
makes these drawable. Same tool frame as the rest of the datasheet; mm.

cd.description: Clearance-diameter limits for tools sweeping the pocket.

maxBottomDiameter.description:
The bottom diameter a terminal tool must not exceed; negative infinity when
unconstrained.

wallLength.description:
The outline a pass around the wall follows, sized for any tool. Absent where the
projection left no outline — a wall nothing can price, not one that is free.

filletRadius.description: Radius of the floor fillet; 0.0 when unfilleted.

filletHeight.description: Height of the floor fillet; 0.0 when unfilleted.

PocketFacts.description: A pocket: a walled space with a floor, and the blend where the two meet.

cd.description: Clearance-diameter limits for tools following the profile.

length.description:
How far the pass travels, mm — the outline's own length. The `radius = 0` term of
`wallLength`, kept because it is what this boundary has always published; prefer the
outline itself, which prices the tool actually used.

wallLength.description:
The outline the pass follows, sized for any tool. Never absent as it is on the other
kinds: the silhouette is what a profile is.

isModified.description: Whether the outline is the part's silhouette or the bridged reading of it.

ProfileFacts.description: A profile: one pass around the part's outline.

horizontalOffset.description: Horizontal distance outward from the feature, in mm, ascending.

verticalOffset.description: How far above the feature the material within that distance rises, in mm, ascending.

ReachCurve.description:
How deep a tool must reach, by how far outboard of the cut the material stands: material
within `horizontalOffset[i]` of the feature rises to `verticalOffset[i]` above it, so
anything on the tool standing that far past its own cutting edge must clear that much.
Both arrays are the same length, ascending, non-negative, in mm; the curve is a
non-decreasing step function, and offsets beyond its last knot clamp to it.

Offsets are measured from the feature, never from the tool's axis: offset zero is the
wall of the cut, so material at offset `d` meets the tool at radius `d` plus the cutting
radius. Each reading is the worst case over the feature's whole surface — the tallest
material within that distance of any point of it, measured above that point.

![A tool cutting a pocket whose wall stands at the cut, with a boss further out: the
horizontal offsets run outward from the feature's edge, the vertical offsets up from
its floor](./media/reach-curve.svg)

The tool checks sweep a tool's shank and holder over this curve; it is here so a
caller can draw it, or sweep an envelope of its own.

center.description:
Where the cone's axis crosses the plane the contours are read in (the tool
frame's) — the sink's position across the part, not along the tool.

innerRadius.description: Radius of the circle the bevel starts from, at its lower edge — the pilot hole.

outerRadius.description: Radius it has opened to at the upper edge.

SinkFacts.description:
A countersink read as a cone of revolution: the circle its bevel starts from and the
one it opens to.

floorArea.description: Surface square to the tool axis, in mm².

wallArea.description: Surface running along it, in mm².

filletArea.description:
The concave rounds between the two, in mm² — as surface, so a quarter round of radius
`r` over a length `L` reads `(π/2)·r·L`, not the `r·L` either projection sees.

contourArea.description: Everything else, in mm²: surfaces with no flat to stand on.

SurfaceAreas.description:
What a feature's surface is made of: every region of it in exactly one bucket, so the five
add up to its surface area and nothing is counted twice.

A description of the feature, not of a pass — see `projectedFloorArea` for the pair that
says what a pass sweeps, and the picture there for how the two families differ. A bucket is
zero where the feature has no such surface. Areas are of the meshed regions, so a curved
surface reads a shade under its exact area.

filletRadius.description:
The blend radius, signed by which way the surface turns: positive rolling over
an edge, negative running into a corner, zero for no blend at all.

maxStepdown.description: The deepest cut taken in one pass down the surface, mm.

surfaceFinishCuspHeight.description: How much scallop the finishing pass may leave between neighboring passes, mm.

isUShapedFillet.description: Whether the fillet has a U-shaped cross section.

hasSharpCorner.description: Whether the surface includes a sharp corner a tool must respect.

useOnlyBallToolsForFinish.description: Whether only ball tools are suitable for the finishing pass.

maxBottomDiameter.description: Largest bottom diameter a terminal tool may have, in mm.

cd.description: Clearance-diameter limits for tools reaching the surface.

toolFit.description: Geometry limits imposed by the surface shape itself.

SurfaceFacts.description:
A three-dimensional surface a tool has to follow rather than sweep; also the surface
half of a chamfer.

spec.description: The dimensional definition of the thread.

process.description: The process used to cut the thread.

Threading.description: A thread a hole is to receive, and how it is to be cut.

ThreadProcess.description: How a thread is to be cut: the three ways there are.

basicDiameter.description: Nominal major diameter of the thread, in mm.

threadPitch.description: Distance between thread crests, in mm.

minMinorDiameter.description: Smallest allowed minor diameter, in mm.

maxMinorDiameter.description: Largest allowed minor diameter, in mm.

minMajorDiameter.description: Smallest allowed major diameter, in mm.

threadPercentage.description: How much of the theoretical thread depth is to be formed, as a percentage.

ThreadSpec.description: The thread a hole is to receive.

atolIgnore.description: Deviation at or below this value is ignored, in mm.

atolDeviate.description: Deviation above the ignored band but at or below this value is reported, in mm.

atolMax.description: Maximum allowed deviation from the model, in mm.

ToleranceBand.description:
How far a machined surface may deviate from the model, in three escalating bands
(`0 <= ignore <= deviate <= max`).

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius the surface shape admits, in mm.

toolDiameter.description: Largest full-diameter tool the surface shape admits, in mm.

toolBottomDiameter.description: Largest bottom diameter the surface shape admits, in mm.

ToolFitResult.description: The tool geometry a surface's own shape admits, before the layers are consulted.

isExternal.description:
The slot runs around material standing in it rather than into the material
around a void.

isClosed.description: The slot's walls close on themselves in plan view.

undercutDepth.description:
How far the groove runs back from its opening, radially; infinite when the slot
could not be measured.

maxEntryCd.description:
The widest tool that can come down through the opening above the slot to reach
it; infinite when nothing above constrains one, zero when nothing fits at all.

cd.description: Clearance-diameter limits for tools machining inside the slot.

filletRadius.description:
Radius of the blend where the slot's walls meet its floor and ceiling; 0.0 when
sharp.

TslotFacts.description:
A t-slot: a groove cut sideways into a wall or around a post, under a ceiling the
machining direction cannot see past.

x.description: Horizontal x coordinate in the current frame.

y.description: Horizontal y coordinate in the current frame.

Vec2.description: A 2D vector (a plain `{ x, y }` object).

cd.description: Clearance-diameter limits for tools machining the wall.

wallLength.description:
The outline a pass around the wall follows, sized for any tool. Absent where the
projection left no outline — a wall nothing can price, not one that is free.

WallFacts.description: A wall: a run of surface square to the tool axis, with no floor of its own.

get.summary: Get the Engine API OpenAPI document

200.description: The exact OpenAPI document served by the Engine API.

ETag.description: An identifier derived from the document bytes.

Cache-Control.description: Cache revalidation policy for the mutable v1 document URL.

post.description: Reports the status of the API key supplied in the Authorization header. A usable key returns 200; a missing, revoked, expired, or unknown key returns 401 — both with the same status body (never problem+json) — so bring-your-own-key integrations can confirm a key and show why it failed.

200.description: The key is active and usable.

401.description: The key is missing, revoked, expired, or unknown.

schema.description: Name of the CAD file you are about to upload. The extension selects the reader, so it must match the file you send: `.step`/`.stp`, `.x_t`/`.x_b`, `.sldprt`, `.catpart`, `.prt`, or `.igs`/`.iges`. Omitting it stores the upload as `.step`, which fails processing for any other format.

parameters.description: Name of the CAD file you are about to upload. The extension selects the reader, so it must match the file you send: `.step`/`.stp`, `.x_t`/`.x_b`, `.sldprt`, `.catpart`, `.prt`, or `.igs`/`.iges`. Omitting it stores the upload as `.step`, which fails processing for any other format.
parameters.name: filename

201.description: The part was created and is ready for direct upload.

get.summary: Download the Autodesk Fusion holder definition
get.description:
Returns the derived holder as Autodesk Fusion writes one: millimetres, segments nose-first,
hyphenated keys.

By default this is a **tool library** (`format=library`) that Fusion can import directly.
`format=document` returns the bare holder document the kernel wrote, which carries the same
geometry but cannot be imported on its own.

The exported envelope stops at the gauge plane by default: material above it is inside the
spindle and cannot collide with anything. Pass `trim=false` for the complete envelope,
including the taper. Both are written by the kernel during the import, so neither is a
reshaping of the other. `trim=true` falls back to the complete envelope for a holder that has
no gauge plane to cut at, or whose taper a flip put at the nose.

An unmeasured gauge length is not written as zero. In a library it becomes the sum of every
segment height — Fusion's own idiom for a holder whose geometry is its gauge length; in a
document the field is omitted, which puts Fusion's own field into manual mode.

get.summary: Export several holders as one Autodesk Fusion library
get.description:
Composes the named holders into a single Autodesk Fusion tool library — how a shop keeps its crib
in one file. Each holder must already have been imported; this reads their stored results and
creates nothing.

Holders appear in the order they were named, and a repeated id is exported once. Each entry
takes its name from the holder’s uploaded filename.

Every named holder has to be exportable. A holder that does not exist, or that has no import
result yet, fails the whole request and is named in the response — a library that silently
contained fewer holders than were asked for would be worse than an error.

schema.description: Comma-separated holder ids, at most 200.

parameters.description: Comma-separated holder ids, at most 200.
parameters.name: ids
